newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS - A Hong Kong executive of French bank Credit Lyonnais was robbed and stabbed to death in his hotel room in Jiangxi province.
-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS - China's air force carried out its largest ever military exercise in the Gobi desert in Xinjiang province a few days ago.
A total of 470,000 troops and 4,000 fighter planes were mobilised.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS - The bronze statue of Queen Victoria in Hong Kong's Victoria Park was deluged with red paint and its face dented with a hammer by a self-proclaimed mainland immigrant artist.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL - Chinese President Jiang Zemin would attend the World Bank and the International Monetory Fund conference held in Hong Kong in September next year.
-- The Xinhua News Agency is trying to raise $600 million to buy a building in Hong Kong's Western District recently acquired by Guangdong Investment.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES - Hong Kong stock market surged with the Hang Seng Index closing 198 points highter at 11,567.90, approaching this year's high.
-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS - China's Ministry of Education has ordered students not to stage "extremist" activities in the run-up to the 65th anniversary of Japan's invasion of China.

-- China is experiencing a "red wave" in the approach of the 60th anniversary of the end of the Long March. The 12,500 kilometre route, now a popular tourist attraction, only offered the local "red rice" in the past to the Red Army. Now, entrepreneurs are marketing it as a health food.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The International Monetary Fund has warned China that failure to improve its tax collection methods would hamper reforms in the state-owned enterprise sector and limit its ability to meet its vast infrastructure programme.
-- Hopewell Holdings confirmed it was in negotiations with a number of parties to sell part or all of its stake in Consolidated Electric Power Asia.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Lane Crawford's Singapore operation registered a $40 million operating loss over the past six months.
